title: Застойная сердечная недостаточность
terminology: Heart disease, murmur, cardiomegaly and congestive heart failure are distinct authored states.
CHF requires clinical congestion such as pulmonary edema, pleural/pericardial effusion, ascites or systemic venous congestion, sometimes with low output.
Cough alone is not cardiogenic pulmonary edema and is commonly respiratory in older small dogs.
Absence of an audible murmur does not exclude feline cardiomyopathy or CHF.
Cardiac phenotype and congestion location remain separate evidence.
Biomarkers support probability and never prove CHF in isolation.
Unstable patients receive oxygen, minimal handling and life-saving drainage/referral before stressful definitive imaging.
POCUS supports triage and effusion/edema probability but does not replace complete phenotype or competing-cause workup.
Home sleeping respiratory rate and weight are longitudinal trends with taught technique, not substitutes for red-flag examination.
Renal, electrolyte and blood-pressure consequences are part of the treatment tradeoff, not optional surprise findings.
No cardiovascular drug, dose, oxygen target, drainage technique or escalation protocol is generated.

commonHistoryQuestions.prompt: Каковы sleeping/resting RR и есть ли dated video?
Есть ли cough, respiratory effort или syncope и когда?
Как менялись appetite, water, urine и weight?
Есть ли prior echo, x-ray, ECG и точный диагноз?
Каков точный список назначений, пропуски и extra doses?
Есть ли collapse, open-mouth breathing, cyanosis или profound weakness?
Есть ли внезапно болезненная холодная конечность или paralysis?
Были ли effusion/drainage, когда и как быстро жидкость вернулась?
Как измеряются RR/weight и каков individual baseline?
Каковы care goals, финансовые ограничения и quality-of-life concerns?

variants.title: Левосторонняя недостаточность с кардиогенным отёком лёгких
variants.diagnosticTruth: Cardiogenic pulmonary edema requires compatible respiratory distress plus congestion evidence and severe cardiac context; cough, murmur, echo or cardiomegaly alone are insufficient.

presentations.complaint: Dog has tachypnea/dyspnea with compatible pulmonary edema and severe cardiac context.

historyAnswers.cough_effort_syncope: Effort dominates; cough alone not used.

followUp.timing: continuous stabilization then congestion/renal/home trend checkpoint

outcomes.safe: Edema improves with verified congestion and ongoing safety monitoring.
outcomes.unsafe: Cough or murmur alone unlocks CHF treatment.

ownerCommunication: Explain the evidence for lung fluid and why cough alone is not enough.

presentations.complaint: Cat with no known murmur presents in acute respiratory distress from occult cardiomyopathy and congestion.

historyAnswers.prior_echo_xray_ecg_diagnosis: No prior phenotype or occult disease.

followUp.timing: continuous respiratory/perfusion then phenotype and home trend

outcomes.safe: Occult cardiomyopathy is diagnosed after low-stress stabilization.
outcomes.unsafe: No murmur falsely excludes heart disease.

ownerCommunication: Explain that cats may have serious heart disease without a previously heard murmur.

presentations.complaint: Previously controlled CHF patient develops recurrent pulmonary edema or compatible relapse.

followUp.timing: acute response then renal/electrolyte/home RR checkpoint

outcomes.safe: Relapse is verified and managed within the original disease trajectory.
outcomes.unsafe: A duplicate patient or random escalation replaces reconciliation.

ownerCommunication: Review the home log and actual containers without moral judgment.

variants.title: Плевральный выпот при сердечной недостаточности или смешанной причине
variants.diagnosticTruth: Pleural effusion may be cardiac or mixed; ventilation impact can require drainage before exhaustive imaging while competing causes remain visible.

presentations.complaint: Cat with pleural effusion has restrictive effort and reduced ventilation.

outcomes.safe: Ventilation improves and cause remains evidence-based.

ownerCommunication: Explain why fluid relief may be needed before the full heart assessment.

presentations.complaint: Effusion requires fluid context and competing-cause assessment despite known or suspected heart disease.

examFindings.finding: Neoplastic, infectious, chylous and other causes remain.

outcomes.safe: Cardiac and competing causes remain separable.
outcomes.unsafe: Known murmur assigns every effusion to CHF.

ownerCommunication: Explain why heart disease can coexist with another cause of chest fluid.

presentations.complaint: Effusion reaccumulates, requiring comfort/ventilation and advanced-control decisions.

historyAnswers.effusion_drainage_history: Date, volume context, response and recurrence rate fixed.

investigations.result: Current fluid restriction and drainage route.

outcomes.safe: Drainage and control decisions follow impact and trajectory.
outcomes.unsafe: Repeated fluid becomes isolated procedures without cause/control plan.

ownerCommunication: Explain when drainage improves breathing and when advanced care is needed.

variants.title: Правосторонняя недостаточность и системный застой
variants.diagnosticTruth: Right-sided CHF requires systemic venous congestion evidence and compatible right-heart/pericardial/pulmonary vascular phenotype while hepatic, protein, neoplastic and other causes remain visible.

presentations.complaint: Ascites, jugular distension, hepatomegaly or systemic edema suggests venous congestion.

examFindings.finding: Liver, protein, neoplastic and other causes remain.

outcomes.safe: Systemic congestion is tied to a compatible phenotype.

ownerCommunication: Explain why abdominal fluid needs both comfort assessment and cause confirmation.

presentations.complaint: Systemic congestion occurs with pulmonary-hypertension, tricuspid or right-heart context.

outcomes.safe: Cardiac and respiratory contributors remain linked.
outcomes.unsafe: Echo label deletes the primary respiratory cause.

ownerCommunication: Explain how lung/vascular disease and the right heart may affect each other.

presentations.complaint: Refractory ascites creates breathing, mobility, appetite and quality-of-life tradeoffs.

examFindings.finding: Refractory label does not close workup.

outcomes.safe: Comfort and organ safety guide advanced decisions.

ownerCommunication: Discuss comfort benefit, recurrence, organ tradeoffs and goals transparently.

variants.title: Острая декомпенсация, аритмия или низкий сердечный выброс
variants.diagnosticTruth: Severe respiratory distress, arrhythmia, hypotension, low output or thromboembolism requires immediate minimal-handling stabilization and ICU/cardiology routes before full phenotype completion.

presentations.complaint: Severe hypoxemic respiratory distress requires hands-off stabilization before definitive phenotype.

outcomes.unsafe: The patient must finish echo/radiographs before oxygen.

ownerCommunication: Explain why stabilization happens before the complete cardiac workup.

presentations.complaint: Dangerous rhythm, syncope, hypotension or cardiogenic shock threatens perfusion.

outcomes.unsafe: A universal cardiovascular drug is generated.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the rhythm and blood pressure determine specialist emergency treatment.

presentations.complaint: Cat with cardiac distress also has sudden painful cold paresed limb or other thromboembolic emergency.

outcomes.safe: Both emergencies remain visible and attributable.
outcomes.unsafe: The limb event detaches from the cardiac episode.

ownerCommunication: Explain the simultaneous heart/lung and limb emergency and uncertainty.

variants.title: Продольный контроль CHF или респираторная имитация
variants.diagnosticTruth: Stable longitudinal control uses taught home trends and renal/BP safety; cough or tachypnea without congestion preserves respiratory, pain, obesity and other mimics.

presentations.complaint: Stable CHF patient returns with sleeping RR and weight log for same-scale control review.

examFindings.finding: Home trend and exam context integrated.

followUp.timing: authored control and safety interval plus red flags

outcomes.safe: Stable control is judged from qualified longitudinal evidence.

ownerCommunication: Verify how RR is counted and explain individual trend-based red flags.

presentations.complaint: Congestion control is complicated by azotemia, electrolyte change or blood-pressure/perfusion concern.

outcomes.safe: Reviewed plan balances breathing and organ perfusion.
outcomes.unsafe: Renal safety disappears or congestion is ignored.

ownerCommunication: Explain the necessary balance and why laboratory/BP rechecks are part of care.

presentations.complaint: Cough or tachypnea occurs with murmur/cardiomegaly but without confirmed congestion.

outcomes.safe: Heart disease and respiratory cause coexist without false CHF.
outcomes.unsafe: Cough plus murmur automatically triggers CHF plan.

ownerCommunication: Explain why heart disease can coexist with a separate cause of cough.

familyValidationRules: Reject if murmur, cardiomegaly, cough, biomarker or echo alone equals CHF.
Reject if lack of feline murmur excludes cardiomyopathy or every effusion is cardiac.
Reject if unstable patient must finish radiographs or echo before oxygen/drainage.
Reject if one clinic RR overrides a taught home trend or renal/electrolyte safety disappears.
Reject if external echo/drainage is instantaneous.
Reject if code generates a cardiovascular drug, dose, oxygen target or drainage technique.
